editorialDeskDispositionResearch.releasePolicy: None of these proposals edits native Scripture or the existing reading candidates, accepts a passage, signs off a literary reading, passes a release gate, or authorizes a merge.

sourceComparisonPhase.scope: Existing original P3 contexts and nine independently displayed connectors; three bridge-attached prefaces are compared only alongside held source trials, never treated as already narrated.
sourceComparisonPhase.applicationPolicy: This worklist only records linked alternatives. Do not alter reading proof, Scripture selection, Bible witnesses, production Atlas or UI based on unapproved variants.
sourceComparisonPhase.witnessNote: All listed comparison anchors resolve in the three installed uncollated witnesses; the adjacent Ruth 2:2 CPDV import gap remains explicitly held. No claims of printed-edition certification.

caseResults.exactSourcePresentationRule: Show genealogical context as editorial. Show the original Noah identity, corruption, ark command, covenant, provisions and obedience before the selected command to enter the ark.
caseResults.requiredOmissionOrAttributionDisclosure: Genesis 6:15–16 dimensions omitted within the held native-source trial; do not imply Genesis 3 to 6 is an uninterrupted episode.
caseResults.heldWithoutPromotionBehavior: If the trial is not selected, retain the visible unresolved ark antecedent; do not claim the missing command to build the ark has been supplied.

caseResults.exactSourcePresentationRule: Retain the selected Passover lamb and observance; display unaltered Exodus 12:29–30 immediately after Exodus 12:27–28 and before the selected Pharaoh release in 12:31.
caseResults.requiredOmissionOrAttributionDisclosure: The source distinction between firstborn judgment occurring and Pharaoh subsequently commanding departure cannot be reduced to one editorial line without losing a causal event.
caseResults.heldWithoutPromotionBehavior: Without the original trial, keep the narrative hinge flagged as incomplete; do not say Pharaoh's reaction was narrated. This fallback does not supply the narrated occurrence of the firstborn judgment between instructions and Pharaoh's order.

caseResults.exactSourcePresentationRule: After the selected death, show the two separate native witnesses consecutively: John 19:31–37 (side, eyewitness and fulfilment), then 19:38–42 (burial), before the selected empty tomb.
caseResults.requiredOmissionOrAttributionDisclosure: The pierced-side witness has separate doctrinal and source status and is not strictly necessary to repair the burial causal gap; avoid treating a full-span trial as one accepted beat.
caseResults.heldWithoutPromotionBehavior: A burial-only exact-source trial restores the tomb antecedent at lower reading cost but leaves the side and fulfilment witness held for separate assessment.

caseResults.exactSourcePresentationRule: Explicitly label the large omitted Acts 16–27 historical interval. If selected, keep a concise editor-attributed Jerusalem arrest and Italy-transfer lead-in; then Acts 28:16 and 17–22 before the existing 28:23 audience.
caseResults.requiredOmissionOrAttributionDisclosure: Acts 28:17–19 already recounts Paul's appeal to Caesar. Remove the repetitive appeal from the editor-owned connector if the whole audience witness is shown; Acts 19:21 is only an intention to see Rome.
caseResults.heldWithoutPromotionBehavior: Acts 28:17–22 alone leaves arrival unanchored; leaving both passages held must not be represented as a continuous historical narrative.

caseResults.exactSourcePresentationRule: Show a visibly non-Scripture shift from Paul's historical Acts ministry to John's apocalyptic vision. Keep the throne/Patmos context separately attributed and avoid implying that Paul witnessed Revelation.
caseResults.requiredOmissionOrAttributionDisclosure: A genre heading needs zero inserted Scripture verses. If Revelation 4:1–2 is trialled, attribute it to John's vision, and do not turn Revelation 1:9–11 into an immediately preceding event.
caseResults.heldWithoutPromotionBehavior: The current genre-labelled editorial context is a viable no-new-verse alternative; without an explicit transition the reader could misread two separate witnesses as a contiguous episode.
